title: Persistence: Supabase and the Showmob API
summary: How Showmob can move from repository JSON and browser-local drafts to secure revisions, media storage and an API without losing portability.

blocks.title: Add memory without trapping the artifact
blocks.body: Supabase can give Showmob durable revisions, identities, permissions and media. The JSON artifact remains the portable language; the database records who may change it, how it evolved and which revision is live.

blocks.title: This is the implementation plan, not a live-data claim
blocks.body: Today, canonical pages still come from repository JSON and Studio drafts stay in browser storage. No Supabase project, schema, authentication flow or API endpoint is introduced by this page.

nodes.title: Request
nodes.detail: A person or authorized agent submits an artifact change.

nodes.detail: The API verifies identity, membership and allowed action.

nodes.detail: The same Showmob runtime contract rejects malformed content.

nodes.title: Revise
nodes.detail: One transaction stores an immutable revision and advances the current pointer.

nodes.title: Render
nodes.detail: The app reads the selected revision and uses the existing renderer.

blocks.heading: Give each Supabase service a narrow job
rows: Artifacts, immutable revisions, series membership, permissions and audit facts
Artifact JSON stays versioned and exportable
Authorization comes from ownership and membership rows, not user-editable metadata
Private by default; type, size, ownership and lifecycle are enforced
Narrow browser reads or draft operations
Explicit grants plus RLS; not the public Showmob contract
Publication, agent writes, validation and multi-record workflows
Secrets stay server-side; service-role access never reaches the browser
Optional collaboration signals after core persistence works
Presence is not a substitute for durable revision history
blocks.caption: Adopt only the services a proven workflow needs. Persistence comes before collaboration effects.

blocks.heading: Separate the artifact from its operating envelope

columns.name: Portable document
columns.detail: The complete schema-versioned Showmob JSON: metadata, theme, series and blocks. It can be exported, reviewed in Git and rendered without Supabase.

columns.name: Persistence envelope
columns.detail: Database IDs, owners, memberships, revisions, audit timestamps, media records and publication state. It makes collaboration safe without leaking into the content language.

blocks.title: Exposure is now an explicit decision
blocks.body: Current Supabase projects may not expose new public-schema tables to the Data API automatically. Showmob must choose the exposed schema, grant only required operations and enable RLS on every exposed table instead of assuming a table is reachable.

blocks.heading: Security gates before the first hosted write

items.label: RLS on every exposed table
items.detail: Policies restrict rows by owner or membership, with both USING and WITH CHECK where updates are allowed.

items.label: Least-privilege grants
items.detail: A role cannot select, insert, update or delete an object unless the product needs that operation.

items.label: Publishable key only in the browser
items.detail: Secret and service-role keys remain in protected server environments because they bypass RLS.

items.label: Private draft media
items.detail: Storage policies bind uploads and reads to the correct owner, project and bucket; public media is a deliberate publication step.

items.label: Immutable revision evidence
items.detail: Every accepted change records who submitted it, when, and which validated document became current.

items.label: Agent writes reviewed like user writes
items.detail: An agent receives scoped authority, never a blanket bypass, and proposed publication remains reviewable.

items.title: Keep GitHub canonical
items.detail: Finish the artifact language and keep the current renderer dependable.

items.title: Prove the round trip
items.detail: Write one validated artifact revision to Supabase, read it back and compare it byte-for-meaning with the exported JSON.

items.title: Add identity and drafts
items.detail: Introduce Auth, ownership and membership policies, then persist private drafts without changing publication.

items.title: Add media
items.detail: Upload constrained files to private Storage and attach reviewed asset records to artifact revisions.

items.title: Open the Showmob API
items.detail: Move publication and authorized agent workflows behind versioned endpoints with validation, audit evidence and idempotency.

items.title: Move reads deliberately
items.detail: Serve hosted artifacts from persistence only after parity, rollback and production observability are proven.

blocks.heading: The API grows around product rules

slides.title: Direct where it is truly simple
slides.body: An owner-scoped draft read can use Supabase's Data API when grants and RLS fully express the rule.

slides.title: Server-side where actions have meaning
slides.body: Publish, archive, accept an agent proposal and advance a revision pointer are product operations. Put them behind Showmob endpoints.

slides.title: Version the public promise
slides.body: Clients should depend on artifact and workflow semantics, not table names. The database can evolve behind the API.

slides.title: Make retries safe
slides.body: Agent and network retries need idempotency keys so one request cannot create duplicate revisions or duplicate uploads.

blocks.heading: Prove one revision before moving the product
blocks.body: The next implementation should create a Supabase development project, write the smallest secure schema, validate one artifact into an immutable revision, read it back and run the existing renderer and contract tests against the result.
